page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. It features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, supported by 32 GB of system memory, which equates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16. This instance operates on a KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average tier. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier multi-core scores in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth also sits in the lower tier, with uncached read speeds of 30.79 GB/sec and write speeds of 25.45 GB/sec. This suggests that while individual threads perform adequately, highly parallelized or memory-bandwidth-intensive workloads may face bottlenecks.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfr7.xlarge offers a memory-optimized resource density. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require a larger memory footprint relative to compute power, but do not demand high multi-threaded throughput or fast local storage. Appropriate workloads include memory-bound applications, small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight text processing or single-threaded execution tasks.
